A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DDOQ research work and are readable throughout, including v2 Appendices A–H and v3 Appendices A–I. Text, equations, figures and tables can be matched despite reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original DDOQ classification, cross-architecture and latent-distance results in Section 4, together with timing measurements in Appendix G.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds a controlled weighting and learning-rate ablation in Appendix I, Table 7.

M1.justification: v2 Algorithm 2 and v3 Algorithm 1 retain the same encoding, clustering, diffusion decoding and weighted-training procedure. Appendix H's square-root weighting heuristic is also unchanged. Appendix I tests alternative weightings without adopting a revised main algorithm.

E1.justification: Both evaluate classification on ImageNet-1K, ImageNette and ImageWoof. The new ablation reuses ImageNet-1K at IPC 10; it adds no dataset, task, population or input-environment scenario.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator sets are unchanged. The new DiT ablation in Table 7 adds explicit comparisons of heuristic DDOQ weighting against a D4M-equivalent constant-weight control and a direct-cluster-weight alternative, neither included in v2's DiT comparison.

E3.justification: Appendix I introduces a controlled protocol using identical clustered DiT images, ImageNet-1K at IPC 10, ResNet-18 teacher and student, and learning rates 0.001, 0.002, 0.005 and 0.01 across three weightings. Existing benchmark settings and Table 6 hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 examines latent Wasserstein distances and example-image weights but leaves alternative variance-reduction choices to future work. v3 adds a focused ablation testing weighting's contribution to classification accuracy and its sensitivity to learning rate. Existing latent-distance and qualitative analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: Both describe five models trained on the same distilled data and retain the existing plus/minus reporting. No changed repetition count, seed policy or uncertainty estimator is established. New Table 7 supplies point estimates without additional run-count or uncertainty information.

E6.justification: Existing classification, generalization, latent-distance and timing values are unchanged. New Table 7 reports, for example, 52.2, 53.6 and 55.6 accuracy at learning rate 0.01 for uniform, heuristic and direct-cluster weighting respectively. v3 replaces the 'around 20%' distance-reduction summary with 15.7% and 16.1%, and omits v2's observation that out-of-class synthetic images can receive high weights.

T1.justification: v3 Section 2.2 adds an explicit time-rescaling reduction to sigma squared(t) = t or beta(t) = 1 and drops v2's stated beta(t) in [0,1) restriction. The central theorem, convergence corollary and appendix proofs are retained; relocated quantization definitions and results are not new theory.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly claims to be the first consistency result for diffusion-based distilled datasets, strengthening the novelty assertion. Its abstract qualifies v2's SOTA claim as 'competitive or SOTA,' and the conclusion similarly moderates performance wording. The underlying theoretical and algorithmic contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: Appendix I adds the qualification that direct-cluster weighting can perform better but requires more careful learning-rate selection. The conclusion explicitly identifies consistency of bi-level and diffusion-guidance frameworks as unresolved. Conversely, v3 removes the concrete warning about highly weighted out-of-class images while retaining the broader distinction between weights and image quality.

D1.justification: Appendix I documents the new ablation's learning-rate grid, fixed-image control and weighting normalization. Existing hardware, timings and main hyperparameters are retained or relocated. However, its 'direct cluster weights' formula uses inverse counts, unlike Algorithm 1's count-proportional weights, leaving the intended implementation of that variant unclear.

R1.justification: v3 removes the discussion and citation of Liu et al.'s 2022 Dataset Distillation via Factorization. It also broadens the positioning from a specific prior work lacking consistency analysis to an explicit claim that no prior dataset-distillation literature addresses this question. Most related work is retained.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and diffusion-background exposition are substantially rewritten. The Contributions subsection is folded into the introduction; definitions, CLVQ material and convergence caveats move into reorganized Appendices B–C; experimental setup moves to Appendix H. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative beyond renumbering.

P2.justification: v3 adopts conference typography and headers throughout, adds a pipeline schematic and Table 7, and relocates the Wasserstein table and CLVQ pseudocode. Tables gain average-reduction and full-accuracy columns. The existing jeep-image panel is retained as Figure 2, rather than constituting new visual evidence.

improvement.justification: The fixed-image ablation provides useful evidence about weighting and learning-rate sensitivity that v2 left unexplored. The pipeline schematic, corrected distance-reduction summaries and qualified performance claims also improve clarity and accuracy. These gains are limited by the ablation's narrow setting, absent uncertainty estimates and inconsistent direct-weight formula. The main method, proofs and benchmark evidence remain essentially unchanged.
